newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Chiluba says Zambia economic reforms irreversible.
newsitem.headline: Chiluba says Zambia economic reforms irreversible.

text.p: Zambian president Frederick Chiluba said on Wednesday that far-reaching economic reforms effected by his government were irreversible.

"The reforms undertaken by my government are unstoppable and will go on. I am sure we will maintain the momentum," Chiluba told a three-day international conference on poverty alleviation organised by the central bank in the capital.
"Even after Chiluba leaves office in 2001, we believe strongly that the same policies will be carried on," he added.
Chiluba said the privatisation of state-run enterprises -- the cornerstone of the reform programme -- was progressing as planned, with some 200 firms sold and some 30 more under negotiation.
"When we complete the privatisation of our most important assets -- Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines -- we will have delivered 85 percent of the economy to the private sector," Chiluba said.
"The sale of the mines is expected to bring in a new surge of investment," he added.
The president encouraged industry to respond to the new economic policies, including the liberalisation of trade, saying any failure to adapt could lead to collapse.
"The reforms are tough. I urge industry to rise to the new challenges. If you respond, you will be on the way to recovery and success," he said.
The president said the ill-conceived economic policies of the 17 years of one-party rule that ended in 1991 had left the majority of Zambians in poverty.
"According to studies, 76 percent of Zambians are extremely poor. Eight percent are moderately poor and only 16 percent are not poor," he said.
Chiluba said the reforms undertaken by his government were bearing fruit, and had seen annual inflation fall to its lowest level in six years in June at 22.7 percent.
The government aims to bring inflation down to around 15 percent by December 1997.
